RE-SCOPED 2026-09-15 by user. Previous scope (receipt delivery via email/WhatsApp/SMS) folded into R-62e. New scope: receipt template versioning + webpage builder for deterministic receipt regeneration.

PROBLEM: receipts are computed on the fly from sale/rental data. The HTML template is hardcoded in receipts.html.js. If the template changes (store name, logo, layout), old receipts would render differently. For backup/system transfer, each receipt must be generated exactly as it was originally.

GOAL: (1) Version receipt templates so each template change is tracked. (2) Provide a visual webpage builder for designing receipt templates with placeholders. (3) Capture a snapshot of each receipt at order time so it can be regenerated deterministically.

ARCHITECTURE:

1. NEW TABLES:
   - receipt_templates: id, name, version (integer), html_content (TEXT, the full HTML/CSS template with {{placeholders}}), block_layout (JSONB, the block arrangement for the builder), is_active (boolean, only one active at a time), created_by (FK users), created_at, updated_at.
   - receipt_snapshots: id, entity_type (SALE|RENTAL), entity_uuid (UUID), template_id (FK), template_version (integer), rendered_html (TEXT, the final frozen HTML), rendered_at (TIMESTAMP). Unique on (entity_type, entity_uuid) â€” one snapshot per order.

2. TEMPLATE BUILDER (webpage builder module):
   - Visual editor with draggable blocks: Header (logo + store name + tagline), Item Table (loop placeholder for line items), Field Row (label + dotted-line value), Text Block (free text), Image (logo/monogram), Divider, Footer (thank-you + signature).
   - Placeholder syntax: {{variable}} resolved at render time.
   - Available placeholders: {{store.name}}, {{store.address}}, {{store.phone}}, {{transaction.number}}, {{transaction.date}}, {{transaction.paymentMethod}}, {{customer.name}}, {{customer.phone}}, {{customer.email}}, {{items}} (loop start), {{/items}} (loop end), {{item.sno}}, {{item.productName}}, {{item.colour}}, {{item.size}}, {{item.quantity}}, {{item.unitPrice}}, {{item.lineTotal}}, {{totals.subtotal}}, {{totals.total}}, {{totals.amountInWords}}, {{totals.itemsCount}}.
   - Live preview panel: renders the template with sample data (hardcoded sample sale).
   - Save as new version: creates a new receipt_templates row with incremented version; old versions remain for historical receipts.
   - CSS is embedded in the template HTML (self-contained, like current branded receipt).

3. SNAPSHOT CAPTURE:
   - After sale/rental commits (in sales.service.js createSale / rental-agreement.service.js createRental), render receipt with the active template and store in receipt_snapshots.
   - delivery_logs.receipt_payload continues to store structured JSON (for email/WhatsApp via R-62).
   - receipt_snapshots.rendered_html stores the final HTML (for deterministic regeneration).

4. DETERMINISTIC REGENERATION:
   - To regenerate a single receipt: fetch receipt_snapshots.rendered_html directly â€” no re-render.
   - For bulk export (backup/transfer): query all snapshots, output HTML files named {sale_number}.html or {agreement_number}.html.
   - Template changes never affect old receipts because snapshots are frozen.

5. API ENDPOINTS:
   - GET /api/receipt-templates â€” list all templates (with version history)
   - POST /api/receipt-templates â€” create new template
   - PUT /api/receipt-templates/:id â€” update template (creates new version)
   - POST /api/receipt-templates/:id/activate â€” set as active template
   - GET /api/receipt-templates/active â€” get current active template
   - POST /api/receipt-templates/preview â€” render preview with sample data
   - GET /api/receipt-snapshots/:entityType/:entityUuid â€” get frozen receipt for an order
   - GET /api/receipt-snapshots/export â€” bulk export all snapshots (admin)

6. FRONTEND:
   - New screen: Receipt Templates (Admin section) â€” list templates, activate, open builder.
   - Template Builder: block-based visual editor with live preview (drag blocks, edit placeholder fields, preview with sample data).
   - Existing ReceiptSection gains a 'View original receipt' button that loads the snapshot.
   - Sale/Rental creation flow unchanged (snapshot captured silently in backend).

7. PERMISSIONS:
   - receipt_templates.view (ADMIN/MANAGER)
   - receipt_templates.manage (ADMIN only â€” create/edit/activate templates)
   - receipt_snapshots.view (ADMIN/MANAGER â€” view frozen receipts)
   - receipt_snapshots.export (ADMIN only â€” bulk export)

SEQUENCING:
  Phase 1: DB schema + template CRUD API + snapshot capture on sale/rental creation.
  Phase 2: Template builder UI (blocks + placeholders + live preview).
  Phase 3: Snapshot viewer + bulk export + integration with existing receipt components.

EPIC. Design doc: docs/COMMUNICATION_PLATFORM.md (read it first). Spec from user 2026-09-14: one platform for ALL customer messages (invoices, birthday offer + wish, stock-availability alerts, festival/new-collection campaigns), provider-replaceable, A/B-ready, AI-ready later.

Provider contract returns {kind:'sent'} or {kind:'handoff', url}. Daily scheduler (Asia/Kolkata, catch-up on late boot, idempotent via dedupe_key) drives birthdays + campaign steps. pg-boss considered and rejected (ledger row is the job).

PHASES: 1 = R-62a..g + i (platform, templates, engine, messages screen, invoice, birthday, stock alerts, preferences). 2 = R-62h campaigns + R-62j analytics. Later = R-62k WhatsApp Cloud API, R-62l SMS, R-62m PDF attachment, R-62n public receipt page + tunnel.

PLANNED 2026-09-10 (god). Human request: use view tables, triggers for grids and dashboard items to reduce DB calls and improve performance. Analysis: FEASIBLE.
Evidence: backend/src/modules/reports/reports.service.js loads whole tables into Node and aggregates in JS (getDashboard = Sale.findAll + reduce, SaleReversal full scan, RentalReturn full scan with 2 nested joins, inventorySnapshot = 4 queries; getTripPnlReport/getVendorSellThroughReport full-table cross-refs; getMarginsReport loads all units into memory). R-28 findings already flag: no SQL pushdown, ~25 unindexed FKs, no date indexes on sold_at/expense_date/start_date, unpaginated lists.
PHASES:
A) GRIDS (sales/rentals/expenses/units/stocks list screens) = regular SQL views (v_sales_grid per-row totalPaise/refundedPaise/units, v_rentals_grid earned/overdue/damage + counts, v_expenses_grid, v_units_grid, v_stocks_grid) + add missing date/FK indexes + LIMIT/OFFSET (or keyset) pagination. Views push join+aggregate into Postgres; the real win for grids is indexes + pagination (overlaps NOD-3 + PG unindexed-FK findings - dedupe at dispatch). List endpoints query views; keep DTO shapes identical.
B) DASHBOARD KPIs + analytics (dashboard, trip P&L, vendor sell-through, stock levels, margins) = materialized view refreshed with REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY OR trigger-maintained incremental summary tables (e.g. reporting_daily keyed by metric_date + dims) maintained by AFTER INSERT triggers on the append-only financial ledger (sales, sale_reversals, rental_returns, expenses). Dashboard endpoint then reads 1-2 indexed rows instead of 5-8 table scans.
CONSTRAINTS:
- Money stays BIGINT paise (JS already BigInt per SEC-H-7); SQL sums must be BIGINT, DTO returns String as today.
- Views/summaries are DERIVED read-only layers, never the source of truth; never mutate completed transactions.
- Reversals are subtracted, not zeroed; R-29 single-reversal partial-unique indexes prevent double-counting in trigger logic.
- Staleness vs cost tradeoff: default MATVIEW CONCURRENTLY refreshed on short interval or day-close.
NOT STARTED. Queued behind running SEC-M/L series + R-31. Manual QA: backend report/dashboard suites stay green; populated-DB latency drop (R-28 notes dev DB empty, absolute timings need seed data).

tasks.title: POS UPI QR checkout flow (Checkout button + Mark received + configurable UPI id)
tasks.details:
POS sale checkout: rename the 'Charge' button to 'Checkout' and add a two-step payment confirmation with a UPI (Unified Payments Interface) QR flow. SALE mode only (rental checkout unchanged this card).

CURRENT (frontend/src/screens/pos/POSScreen.jsx): the 'Charge' button (line ~700) calls handleCheckout which creates the sale immediately and shows the receipt. Payment method comes from the payment-methods picklist Select (paymentMethod state, default 'Cash').

NEW FLOW:
1. Rename sale-mode button 'Charge' -> 'Checkout'. Keep 'No permission' when SALES.CREATE absent.
2. Clicking Checkout opens a Payment step (a Dialog/panel) INSTEAD of creating the sale. The sale is created only on 'Mark received'. Move the current handleCheckout create-sale logic into the confirm handler; keep the SEC-M-3 checkoutKeyRef idempotency (one key per intent, reused on retry, reset after success/clear).
3. If paymentMethod === 'UPI': show a UPI QR encoding the checkout amount. Show the amount clearly. Buttons: 'Mark received' (primary) + 'Cancel'. Customer scans -> cashier taps 'Mark received' -> create the sale -> replace the QR area with a 'Thank you' confirmation, then reveal the existing SaleReceipt + 'New transaction'.
4. If paymentMethod === 'Cash' (or any non-UPI): no QR. Show the amount + 'Mark as received' + 'Cancel' -> create the sale -> 'Thank you' -> receipt.
5. 'Cancel' in the payment step returns to the cart without creating a sale (idempotency key preserved so a re-open reuses it).

UPI QR CONTENT: encode the standard deep link upi://pay with params: pa=<VPA> (required), pn=<payee, use SHOP_NAME 'SHREE Fashion Store' from components/ShopLogo.jsx or the account label>, am=<amount in rupees, 2dp from totalPaise>, cu=INR, tn=<note e.g. 'SHREE Fashion Store sale'>, tr=<txn ref>. Sale number does NOT exist yet (sale is created on Mark-received), so use the checkout idempotency key (checkoutKeyRef) as tr and in tn. Build the string in a tested pure helper (e.g. platform/upi.js buildUpiUri) and URL-encode each value.

UPI ID CONFIGURABLE FROM PICKLIST: add a new flat picklist 'UPI accounts' (mirror the payment-methods module + R-33 expense-types), but each entry needs TWO fields: label + vpa (the VPA / UPI id, e.g. shree@okhdfcbank) + is_active. So the model/migration/validation carry a vpa column and FlatPicklistManager (or a small dedicated manager) must support the extra field/column. Mount /api/picklists/upi-accounts (read=authenticate, write=PICKLISTS.CREATE/UPDATE). Seeder optional (may seed a placeholder VPA or leave empty). POS reads the active UPI account(s): if one -> use it; if several -> small selector in the payment step; if none -> disable the UPI path / show 'Add a UPI account in Picklists' hint.

QR RENDERING: no QR lib is installed. Add a pinned dependency (qrcode or qrcode.react) and verify it builds under vite 8 / react 19; render the upi:// string as a QR (canvas/svg/dataURL). Keep bundle impact reasonable.

BACKEND: only the new upi-accounts picklist module (model+migration ESM export+validation+routes+controller, register in models/index.js, mount in app.js, run on impoc_dev). NO change to sale creation and NO payment-gateway verification — 'Mark received' is a manual human confirmation.

TESTS: buildUpiUri unit test (params + encoding); PaymentDialog tests (UPI shows QR + Mark received -> thank you -> receipt; Cash shows no QR); backend upi-accounts module tests mirroring payment-methods. Frontend vitest + build + backend jest green.

BOUNDARIES/SEQUENCING: SALE mode only. Depends on R-33 (soft): both edit picklistsApi.js + PicklistManagementScreen.jsx, so sequence AFTER R-33 integrates to avoid merge conflicts. Leave changes UNCOMMITTED for god to verify+integrate. PLAN ONLY for now — do not dispatch until the human says go.

=== AMENDMENT (2026-09-10, user): add a PUBLIC customer-facing display page on a SEPARATE DEVICE (tablet/phone facing the customer). Chosen over same-browser BroadcastChannel, so it needs a public backend live channel. ===

PAIRING: POS shows a short non-guessable display code (e.g. 6 chars), persisted per terminal in localStorage so it stays stable. The customer device opens /display/:code (or enters the code on /display).

BACKEND (new ephemeral, in-memory — no DB): a POS-display channel keyed by code.
- POST /api/pos-display/:code (AUTHENTICATED, SALES.CREATE) — POS publishes the current payment state {status:'idle'|'awaiting'|'received', method:'UPI'|'Cash', amountPaise, upiUri}. Keep the payload MINIMAL: status, method, amountPaise, upiUri only. NO customer PII, NO cart lines.
- GET /api/pos-display/:code/stream (PUBLIC, NO AUTH) — Server-Sent Events stream the display subscribes to (EventSource). On connect, immediately send the current state (late-join); push every update. Heartbeat comments keep it alive; clean up subscriber on close. In-memory Map<code,{state,subscribers}> (lost on restart — fine, state is ephemeral).
- SECURITY: only SUBSCRIBE is public and it exposes just amount + upiUri + status for an active checkout (payment-facing info a customer sees anyway). Publish is auth-gated so nobody can inject a fake QR. Code is random + state resets to idle after received/timeout to limit enumeration. Note this in the PR.

FRONTEND:
- Restructure App.jsx: today ALL routes sit inside RouteGuard+AppShell. Add a top-level Routes split so /display and /display/:code render OUTSIDE RouteGuard+AppShell (full-screen, no nav chrome, no auth). The guarded app stays the catch-all.
- Display page (public): opens EventSource to /api/pos-display/:code/stream and renders states with framer-motion (already a dep): IDLE = pleasant ambient/branded animation ('waiting for next customer'); AWAITING+UPI = large UPI QR (rendered from the upiUri in the payload) + amount 'Scan to pay Rs X'; AWAITING+Cash = amount + 'Please pay at the counter' (no QR); RECEIVED = remove QR, thank-you animation, then auto-return to IDLE after a few seconds. Auto-reconnect on drop (EventSource default).
- POS side (payment step from the base task): generate/show the display code (with a link/QR to open the display device), and POST the state to /api/pos-display/:code on every transition — checkout-UPI -> awaiting+UPI+amount+upiUri; checkout-cash -> awaiting+Cash+amount; mark-received -> received; cancel/clear/new transaction -> idle. POS still builds the upiUri (VPA from the UPI-accounts picklist) so the display needs no picklist/auth access — it just renders what it is sent.

TESTS: SSE endpoint (publish updates a subscriber; late-join gets current state; publish requires auth, subscribe does not); display page renders each state from mocked EventSource messages; POS posts state on transitions.

This REPLACES the earlier 'BroadcastChannel same-browser' idea. Still PLAN ONLY — do not dispatch until the human says go.

tasks.title: Barcode values: SHREE prefix + timestamp + counter (unique across sequence resets)
tasks.details:
PROBLEM: generated barcode values are a bare reflection of the DB sequence barcode_seq (12-digit zero-padded). If the sequence is dropped/reset (db wipe, re-migrate) the counter restarts at 1 and NEW labels collide with labels already printed and stuck on stock. User also wants every barcode to start with 'shree'.

DECISION (user, 2026-09-13): value = 'SHREE' + TS6 + CNT4 = 15 chars, uppercase A-Z0-9 only.
- TS6: seconds since 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, base-36, zero-padded to 6 (valid until ~2094; formatter throws after). One timestamp per generate call.
- CNT4: nextval(barcode_seq) mod 36^4, base-36, zero-padded to 4 (1,679,616 per second >> max batch 100 pages x 10x10 grid = 10,000).
- Uniqueness argument: collision needs same second AND same counter; within a second the sequence keeps climbing so counters differ; after a sequence reset the timestamp is strictly later than every printed label. Only a backwards system clock could break it (accepted).
- Example: SHREE0D4MWO0001.

SCOPE:
1. barcode.service.js: new formatBarcodeValue(seq, nowMs) + BARCODE_FORMAT constants (prefix, epoch, lengths) in barcode.constants.js; replace 12-digit padStart; drop the 999999999999 cap.
2. Migration: widen units.barcode, sale_lines.barcode, rental_lines.barcode VARCHAR(12)->VARCHAR(32); replace units_barcode_length_check (1..32). Postgres refuses ALTER TYPE on a column used by a view, so the migration DROPs the 5 R-32 grid views, alters, then re-creates them by importing VIEWS from 20260910000002-create-grid-views.js. ESM export style (const migration = {...}; export const up = ...).
3. Models Unit/SaleLine/RentalLine STRING(12)->STRING(32).
4. Validators max(12)->max(32): units.validation (barcodeSchema), sales.validation, rental-agreement.validation (x2), intake/stock.validation.
5. Tests: update barcode.integration 12-digit expectations to the new format; add unit tests for formatBarcodeValue (prefix, length, charset, monotonic, wrap).
